market.title: Wet Market
market.subtitle: Buy fresh produce and bargain a little.
market.culture: Wet markets (菜市场) price goods by the 斤 (jīn, about 500 grams). Bargaining is common at street stalls, but not in supermarkets. Produce here is usually cheaper than in shops.

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.text: 你好，要点什么？西红柿很新鲜。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, yào diǎn shénme? Xīhóngshì hěn xīnxiān.
dialogue.en: Hello, what would you like? The tomatoes are very fresh.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Xīhóngshì duōshǎo qián yī jīn?
dialogue.en: How much is a jin of tomatoes?

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Wǔ kuài yī jīn.
dialogue.en: Five yuan per jin.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Piányi diǎn, lái liǎng jīn.
dialogue.en: Make it cheaper, and give me two jin.

choices.en: Can you make it a little cheaper?

words.en: Can you / Is it possible to

choices.en: How much is this?

choices.pinyin: Gěi wǒ chēng yī jīn píngguǒ.
choices.en: I'd like a jin of apples, please.

supermarket.title: Supermarket
supermarket.subtitle: Find products and pay at checkout.
supermarket.culture: In Chinese supermarkets plastic bags are charged, usually a few mao up to one yuan. You can bring your own bag or buy one at checkout. WeChat Pay and Alipay are accepted everywhere.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, qǐngwèn niúnǎi zài nǎlǐ?
dialogue.en: Hello, where is the milk?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Zài lěngguì qū, jìn mén yòu zhuǎn.
dialogue.en: It's in the refrigerated section, turn right when you enter.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Xièxie. Zhège duōshao qián?
dialogue.en: Thank you. How much is this?

dialogue.speaker: cashier
dialogue.text: 二十三块八。塑料袋要吗？三毛。
dialogue.pinyin: Èrshísān kuài bā. Sùliàodài yào ma? Sān máo.
dialogue.en: Twenty-three yuan and eighty cents. Would you like a plastic bag? It's thirty cents.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

choices.en: I'd like a bag, please.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

Is there a discount?

convenience-store.title: Convenience Store
convenience-store.subtitle: Grab a drink and heat up a snack.
convenience-store.culture: Convenience stores like 7-Eleven, FamilyMart and Lawson are everywhere, often open 24 hours. They sell hot food such as 包子 and 饭团, and many have free microwaves and small seating areas.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, mǎi yī píng shuǐ.
dialogue.en: Hello, I'd like to buy a bottle of water.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Yào chángwēn de háishì bīng de?
dialogue.en: Would you like it at room temperature or cold?

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 冰的。这里有微波炉吗？我想加热。
dialogue.pinyin: Bīng de. Zhèlǐ yǒu wēibōlú ma? Wǒ xiǎng jiārè.
dialogue.en: Cold, please. Is there a microwave here? I'd like to heat it up.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu, zài ménkǒu nàbiān.
dialogue.en: Yes, it's over there by the door.

choices.en: How much is the total?

choices.text: 可以帮我加热一下这个饭团吗？
choices.pinyin: Kěyǐ bāng wǒ jiārè yīxià zhège fàntuán ma?
choices.en: Could you heat this rice ball for me?
Do you have any hot steamed buns?

clothes-store.title: Clothes Store
clothes-store.subtitle: Find your size and try it on.
clothes-store.culture: Chinese clothing sizes run smaller than Western ones — a medium may fit like a small. Always try on if possible. Return policies are stricter than in the West, so keep the tags and your receipt.

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, xiǎng kàn diǎn shénme?
dialogue.en: Hello, what would you like to see?

words.en: to look / to watch / to read

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu yǒu M mǎ ma?
dialogue.en: Do you have this in size M?

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu de, shìyījiān zài nàbiān.
dialogue.en: Yes, the fitting room is over there.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 好的，我试一下。会不会太小？
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, wǒ shì yīxià. Huìbùhuì tài xiǎo?
dialogue.en: Okay, I'll try it on. Will it be too small?

choices.en: Do you have a size larger?

choices.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yǒu bié de yánsè ma?
choices.en: Do you have this in other colors?
I won't try it on. I'll buy it directly.

shoe-store.title: Shoe Store
shoe-store.subtitle: Ask for your size and try the shoes.
shoe-store.culture: Chinese shoe sizes use the European (mm) system, so a 42 is usually close to your home size. Walk around in the shoes before buying — comfort matters.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, zhè shuāng xié yǒu 42 mǎ ma?
dialogue.en: Hello, do you have this pair of shoes in size 42?

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu de, nǐ shì shì.
dialogue.en: Yes, try them on.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒudiǎn jǐn. yǒu méiyǒu dà yī mǎ?
dialogue.en: It's a bit tight. Do you have a larger size?

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu de, gěi nǐ sìshísān mǎ.
dialogue.en: Yes, we do. Here’s a size 43 for you.

choices.en: Do you have any other styles?
Can I get a discount?

souvenir-shop.title: Souvenir Shop
souvenir-shop.subtitle: Pick up tea, silk and gifts.
souvenir-shop.culture: Souvenir shops near scenic spots are pricier, and bargaining is expected. For tea and silk, buy from reputable shops and ask for a receipt. Airport shops are convenient but more expensive.

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.text: 你好，看看纪念品吗？茶叶、丝绸都有。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, kànkan jìniànpǐn ma? cháyè, sīchóu dōu yǒu.
dialogue.en: Hello, would you like to see some souvenirs? We have tea and silk.

dialogue.en: It’s 180 yuan for a box.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Tài guì le, piányi diǎn ba.
dialogue.en: It’s too expensive. Can you lower the price?

night-market.title: Night Market
night-market.subtitle: Try cheap street food at the stalls.
night-market.culture: Night markets (夜市) offer cheap street food, usually paid by QR code. Portions like 十串 come as counted skewers. Go where the queues are long — that's a sign the food is fresh.

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.text: 你好，要什么？烤串、臭豆腐都有。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐhǎo, yào shénme? Kǎochuàn, chòudòufu dōu yǒu.
dialogue.en: Hello, what would you like? We have skewers and stinky tofu.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Wǒ yào shí chuàn kǎoròu.
dialogue.en: I’d like ten skewers of roasted meat.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, èrshí yuán. Yào là ma?
dialogue.en: Okay, twenty yuan. Do you want it spicy?

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Yào yīdiǎn là. Zài nǎlǐ děng?
dialogue.en: A little spicy, please. Where should I wait?

refund-exchange.title: Returns & Exchanges
refund-exchange.subtitle: Send back or swap what you bought.
refund-exchange.culture: To return or exchange goods in China you usually need the receipt and original tags, within about 7 days. Refunds to Alipay or WeChat take a few days to reappear; an in-store exchange is usually easier than a cash refund.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐhǎo, zhè jiàn yīfú wǒ xiǎng tuì.
dialogue.en: Hello, I’d like to return this piece of clothing.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu xiǎopiào ma? Mǎi le duōjiǔ le?
dialogue.en: Do you have the receipt? How long ago did you buy it?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 昨天买的，穿不了。这是小票。
dialogue.pinyin: Zuótiān mǎi de, chuān bùliǎo. Zhè shì xiǎopiào.
dialogue.en: I bought it yesterday, but it doesn’t fit. Here’s the receipt.

dialogue.speaker: clerk
dialogue.text: 好的，可以换。退款退到付款账户。
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, kěyǐ huàn. Tuìkuǎn tuì dào fùkuǎn zhànghù.
dialogue.en: Okay, you can exchange it. The refund will go to your payment account.

choices.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yī gè yánsè.
choices.en: I'd like to change to a different color.
When will the refund arrive?
What should I do if I lost the receipt?

mall-navigation.title: Finding Your Way in a Mall
mall-navigation.subtitle: Ask where restrooms and food are.
mall-navigation.culture: Chinese shopping malls are multi-story, with food courts usually on the top floor. Restrooms and baby-care rooms are common, and asking the information desk (服务台) is reliable.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 你好，请问洗手间在哪里？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐhǎo, qǐngwèn xǐshǒujiān zài nǎlǐ?
dialogue.en: Hello, where is the restroom?

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.text: 在二楼，坐扶梯上去右转。
dialogue.pinyin: Zài èr lóu, zuò fútī shàngqù yòu zhuǎn.
dialogue.en: It's on the second floor. Take the escalator up and turn right.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.text: 请问电梯在哪里？我推了婴儿车。
dialogue.pinyin: Qǐngwèn diàntī zài nǎlǐ? Wǒ tuī le yīng'érchē.
dialogue.en: Excuse me, where is the elevator? I have a stroller.

dialogue.speaker: staff
dialogue.pinyin: Diàntī zài nàbiān, zhí zǒu.
dialogue.en: The elevator is over there. Go straight ahead.

choices.en: Which floor is the food court on?
Where is the exit?
Where is the service desk?

electronics-store.title: Electronics Store
electronics-store.subtitle: Buy a charger or data cable.
electronics-store.culture: Electronics markets and phone shops sell cables and chargers for every phone type. Prices are negotiable at markets but fixed at brand stores. Bring your phone so staff can confirm the connector.

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐhǎo, yǒu shǒujī chōngdiànqì ma?
dialogue.en: Hello, do you have a phone charger?

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.text: 有。你什么手机？安卓还是苹果？
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu. Nǐ shénme shǒujī? Ānzhuó háishì píngguǒ?
dialogue.en: Yes. What kind of phone do you have? Android or iPhone?

dialogue.speaker: you
dialogue.pinyin: Píngguǒ, hái yào yī gēn shùjùxiàn.
dialogue.en: iPhone, and I also need a charging cable.

words.en: to want / to need / to request

dialogue.speaker: seller
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo de, yī tào bāshí yuán.
dialogue.en: Okay, it's eighty yuan for a set.

choices.en: Does it have fast charging?
Can I try it out?
How long is the warranty?
